title: Great but bugs
body: This app is great and helps me remember meds and get ready for the day much faster. The gamification aspect is awesome. But there are some issues. Often when I scroll down to re-order tasks, I get a blank window popping up with nothing but the cancel and done buttons. So I just delete tasks. Also, today I was running a routine and closed my ph. When I re-opened the app, the routine I was working on was gone but I was still getting notifications that time was running out on my task. When I clicked on a notification, it didn’t take me back to that routine so I had to restart the whole thing again. Finally, ph notifications are important so we remember to open the app. But I find it disruptive when the app dings to tell me time is running out AND my ph gets a notification about it. I always have to stop to see if it’s a work email. Bonus ideas: Some of us are chronically ill. It’d be awesome if we could select a sick/slow/relaxed routine option. So if we wake up unwell one day, instead of starting a routine on schedule and completing it in time, perhaps we could have a “sick day” routine saved somewhere that is not attached to the calendar. So whenever we’re ready to get moving, we click on that routine and instead of each task being timed, we could set the app to give us a gentle reminder every 10/15/30 mins to check the routine and get back into it. Whatever interval the person needs. Sick days are hard enough without feeling like a failure but this app would be amazing in a sick day coz we can get it to do remind us of the extra symptom-management tasks. Also, the app is advertised to have on demand routines. I get that we can click a routine and start it any time, but do we have to create routines and allocate them to a particular time? That’s all I managed to do. I want a “going out” routine so when I have to leave the house, I can make sure I get all my meds, charge my wheelchair, etc. But I don’t always know ahead of time if I’m going out so I don’t want to assign it to a spot in the calendar. Overall though, this app is a game changer!
author: JessicaH2

title: Life-changing
body:
This app has literally changed my life. I’m 25 and I have ADHD, so it help remind me of things just I normally forget about. More significantly, it helps me try not to do everything all at the same time, and get overwhelmed! Doing one thing at a time is so helpful. 

My room now stays consistently clean, and I have broken down the cooking process so that I put all my ingredients before hand and the kitchen stays orderly while I cook and there’s isn’t a mess spread over the whole kitchen. 

You can tell that a lot of thought and design have gone into this app to make if ADHD user friendly. So thank you for caring about us and making this app. 

I would also love to see some extra features added too. If the routine is set to “ends by” instead of “starts by”, it auto re-calculates the time but it does it in a really weird way that doesn’t make any sense to me and I don’t know how it’s re-calculating it. It would be great if it doesn’t re-calculate the times, but it just showed you what time you would be finished your routine if you continued at this rate (i.e. very late), and how much time you have to catch up on to be finished on time. Therefore, the goal would be to continue trying to reduce that overtime and do things faster. And as you got faster, your estimated finish time would be earlier and the “how many minutes late are you” time would hopefully be smaller. 

Also, the app has a really good chime sound at about 3/4 of the way through a task. But sometimes the chime sound doesn’t go off and it’s just the regular other sounds and I don’t really know why it doesn’t go off. So it would be great to have that time sound all the time on all of the tasks.

Also, if you made an Apple Watch version, I would buy an Apple Watch.

title: Works well, new features would be great though

This app has helped me so much to remember to brush my teeth, wash my face etc, and still leave my house on time to go to university.
Iʼm so glad this app exists and would recommend to any friends who need help staying on track. 

Some suggestions:
- it’d be great if it was an Apple Watch compatible visual timer, as I have to bring my phone with me from my bedroom to my kitchen to my bathroom when Iʼm getting ready in the morning, as I really benefit from glancing at the timer. 
- it’d be cool if a desktop version could be made. 

I understand developing such a great tool would be difficult, I would love to know if I can donate somewhere.

~Thank you ☆

title: Great interface, but needs to time tasks and record it
body: Love the interface and I really wanted this app to work for me, but I need to be able to keep track of how long it actually takes me to do tasks and keep records so I can adjust my routine. Having a poor sense of how long it takes to complete tasks is a huge part of time blindness. The negative number when you go overtime isn’t helpful either, it would be much more helpful to have the total time (or both) you’ve spent on the task so far but in red. Another useful feature that other apps have is being able to set the end time for the routine and the start time adjusts automatically. It would also be nice to have some sort of sidebar overview of the entire routine that is visible while doing the routine.  For this reason, I’ll be sticking with the Routinist app for now even though its interface isn’t as appealing.

title: Amazing app, but still pretty basic
body:
I use Brili daily to start up my day, and regularly for other things as well. The routines are a great way to ensure I don’t waste my day with a slow start and ensure I’m on time when there’s somewhere I need to be. Brili can adjust the time I have for each task based on the time I have left. If I oversleep I’ll have less time per step, but if I finish tasks quickly then the time I have for other tasks increases again. I haven’t found an app that is even close to as effective as Brili, nor any that do anything remotely similar.

So why not 5 stars? There’s a problematic lack of information (a tutorial and the app description. There’s no information on, for example, sharing routines and your subscription between devices) and the app itself is pretty basic (but still in development, so that could well be fixed over time). 

There’s a few annoying features. You can only turn notifications on or off. Turning them on means you’ll be spammed with them until they lose all meaning. Minimum times are useful to ensure Brili doesn’t shorten important tasks too much, but if you happen to be done earlier (or just forgot to swipe away a previous task), you’ll need to wait out the minimum time or skip the task.

There’s also some features that aren’t that annoying but could be better. No clear distinction is made between completed routines and skipped routines, and routine management is a bit lacking. You can’t sort or filter routines, small variations (like leaving half an hour later) require you to duplicate the routine, and you can only plan routines to specific days of the week. It’s perfectly fine for people with very regular schedules, but can be annoying for people with irregular shifts.

title: AuDHD lifesaver
body: My kids and I are AuDHD. A doctor once remarked that my kids, on the highest dosage of ADHD medication allowed for their size, seemed entirely unmedicated. In other words, we got it bad bad. They’re brilliant kids that have taught themselves coding, piano, physics, etc. but can’t be on time to save their life. I’m the same way. Brili is somehow the only thing that has ever worked perfectly for us. It creates the urgency and momentum we need to get moving and stay moving, and has the novelty and stimulus to keep us all on track. It’s a deceptively simple app, but is incredible for getting kids (or adults) to just do the damn thing already. We’ve been using it since they were 6 and 8 and now they’re 18 and 20 and they still use it to get to class on time. I use it to get out of bed in the morning without scrolling, to leave the house on time, and to get started on a workout routine without procrastinating.

author: Shows blank when it’s not

title: ALMOST perfect, glitch found with suggestions made. Actually SO helpful for ADHD, shockingly!!
body:
I love this app, it helps a ton for routines as someone who has ADHD. It’s the ONLY tool that I have consistently used and gives me a visual idea of how long it’ll take me to get ready. I learned this from Jessica @HowToADHD, and it’s fantastic ❤️ I pay for it yearly and it’s worth every penny.

NOTICED GLITCH:

Another person mentioned it, but if you try to swipe to switch order of your items in the current routine.. they get stuck on top of each other or the next one disappears altogether until you swipe the current one away.

I have a few suggestions, though. I emailed the developer, but they didn’t get back:

1. Give different tone options for the reminders. The standard one triggers rage in me and I have to mute it, which defeats the purpose of it.

2. Give us the ability to edit the end time while routine is already started.

3. Give the ability to remove steps of the routine after already started without switching the order around to put the one you want to remove at the front.

4. Create more intrusive notifications on the reminders of the routine scheduled to start. Maybe create a way for it to add an alarm on your phone.

5. Have the app retain history of how long you have taken on a task in the past and suggest a new timing to make more efficient. Have the suggestion be a range of timing, suggest an average or longest time!

author: ellimac1232

title: Doesn’t sync with extra devices
body:
If you’re going to charge $50 per year for your app, you ought to provide the ability to set a routine on one device (like an iPad or MacBook) and execute the routine on another device (like an iPhone). Instead there appears to be no way to use the same user id across multiple devices. Without that capability, this app is overpriced garbage. With that capability, it would actually be worth paying for since it’s a good idea in principle, just deployed terribly.

Having said that, the routine suggestions are top notch. I recommend making note of some of your favorite routines from this app and implementing them in another routine tracking app that is more affordable and has multi-device functionality.

title: Solid 3 1/2 lots of potential
body:
This app is loaded with good potential. It’s a great idea and truly does work to get my scatty brain to do the things. I like the premade routines and that you can modify them to fit what you need. 

Now the things that I truly hope they improve. It’s a $50/ year app but it feels a little bit like they’re still beta testing. I can’t tell you how many times I’ve finished the last thing on the routine list and marked it done but then closed the app and went on with my day and didn’t wait around for the final screen to come around. The next time I open the app it’s still there, saying I didn’t finish it. When I re-finish it, it puts on the calendar that I finished my go to bed routine at 6:30 am the following day. Also, you’re supposed to be able to rearrange your tasks in your routine while you’re in the routine but this has never worked for me despite multiple tries. Finally, if you take longer to finish your routine than normal, when you finish it, your end time is right on the calendar but your start time is not. 

Honestly, it seems like a ton of money for what it does. Like way too much. But it’s the only app I know of that does what it does so I guess you have to pay what they ask. Maybe I should have done more research.
author: Babs2225

title: Unaffordable
body: I found this app and was curiously excited to use it. I went in and added all the routines I currently have and was excited to add more. Slightly geeked out setting them up because I love adding color coding/icons/etc to anything. I have severe combined ADHD and really loved this at the beginning. I used it for about a week before one day, I went to open the app and I’m suddenly blocked by a paywall. Can’t even access or see any of my routines. I’ve seen the developers responses to this exact complaint and it appears that they feel this is completely justified. I don’t think the app is truly worth the price listed ($8 monthly or $50 yearly) considering the plethora of issues and lack of options noted in the other negative reviews. Feels greedy in my opinion, and reiterates the same sentiment that rings true in so many areas throughout our country (USA) that if you don’t have money to shell out, you don’t deserve to function well. I’ve deleted the app and will continue looking for something more affordable and useful.
author: Scooter0330

title: I’d change one thing
body: I’m loving this app so far. I’ve tried many routine apps, but I really enjoy the UI of Brili Routines. Easy to use. Easy to build your own routines and adjust pre-existing Brili routines to your needs. The one thing I’d change is that if you postpone a task in your routine that the time you’ve spent on it doesn’t get reset to zero. I could see how some users might want it to be reset, so in that case maybe there could be a choice in the settings for each user to decide for themselves.
author: Colorfulcolorado

title: Almost everything
body:
This app is almost everything I need. I’m surprised that there are no other apps like this except Fabulous which is just WAY too busy! All I want is routines!  

I lose track of time much less with this app. But I still do lose track, especially because the start and est end times are very small. I also wish there was a current time clock easily visible during a routine. 

Also, the green color is not very appealing . If I could just change the color, that would go a long way for my experience. 

And widgets would be huge, but I know that’s a big ask. 

Because I still lose track of time even with the help of brili, I have been considering just using a habit app widget and multi timer widget on a Home Screen
author: LibertyLikes

title: Won't adjust time
body: The app won't adjust time for tasks if one took a little longer like the kids app.  It changes the end time.  If I forget to swipe and keep going, it won't let me swipe two. I just have to delete. How do I fix this or I may ask for my money back.
author: Jengirlmama

title: I heard this app works well with people with ADHD, I disagree strongly
body:
I have tried many apps and the accessibility of this app is really poor.
1. You do not make an account therefore you cannot use it on multiple devices or even share it to other devices. I installed it on my Ipad and set everything up (which took hours) and I realized that my phone will not be able to even see it. 
2. When I was told I could share routines and that would fix my issue I tried it. Nothing happened. 
3. There is no Widget so you can visavlly see what your routine is or any reminder. 
4. You have to be the one to go into the app and it only does the things on there.
5. The icons are irritating to find and many are put under random words. 
6. The icons cannot have their color changed. 
Overall if you have ADHD and need to be prompted and reminded to do something. This app will work as poorly for you as it was to me. A lot of work needs to go into this before it should be labeled as ADHD friendly.
author: Emajean Lou

title: Apple Watch
body: I love this routines app. And, I have tried them all. My only issue is that I really need to have it on my watch. That's why I always go back to Routinery. Which is a good app too- but not as good as this one. Please make watch compatible! Thank you so much! Will change to five stars! I really do love this app. Thank you.
author: PhoebeKate87

title: Fantastic concept with imperfect execution
body:
After only a few days I can say that so far, this has been a super effective and helpful tool for me, and I am actually considering purchasing a subscription when the trial is up (which is a huge deal for me because I generally do not purchase subscriptions for apps, unless it is something that is particularly useful for me). However, I have found a few things that are buggy or not quite as convenient as I would have hoped, which is the reason I give this product 4 stars rather than 5.

Concept/overall effectiveness of this type of tool for me: 5 stars (not to be dramatic but to say it’s been potentially life-changing after a pretty short time may be appropriate)

Execution/app design: 4 stars - there are a few things that I think could be a little more convenient or user-centric but overall pretty good

Programming: maybe 3.5 stars - I’ve found a few things that are a little buggy or picky about the movements required to execute a particular task. I’m not a professional programmer, but I have a degree in electrical engineering and I’ve programmed various things. I’m not overly impressed with the programming compared to similar apps or even feel like I could have programmed it  better (realizing that it may be harder to get some of the features right than I’m envisioning, but I’m still not impressed).

Price point/value: 4 stars (not based on comparing it to other available stuff, but just the value for the product itself based on cost per year feels slightly higher than I would like to see both from the perspective of being on a student budget, terms of affordability or financial accessibility for more people who would benefit from this, but overall not too bad and I am considering purchasing a subscription if I don’t find an alternative similar product that works almost as well for my needs. It would be nice to see different “tiers” for different budgets as well - for example basic or intermediate versions that you can purchase for different prices that perhaps limit the number of routines and/or routine tasks you can enter with the pro or unlimited version available for people with the budget for the full subscription fee.

Overall great app, but I would like to see various improvements, such as making the swiping for tasks less sensitive, an “undo” option to bring a completed or deleted task back, ability to create subroutines or break tasks down into subtasks for worse brain days, reorder a bunch of tasks on the list more efficiently in the middle of a routine or add/delete tasks from the routine list for the current day during the routine, change the time limit for a tasks or whether you earn the stars for a task during the routine or afterward, edit your star total or stars earned by adding or subtracting manually, “choose your adventure” style forks in the routine, set in advance optional tasks and whether or not a task can be skipped or done in less time if you’re running late (e.g. I want to be able to set minimum and maximum time estimates for the routine or tasks that can be done faster, and if I woke up late I want to be able to have presets/settings that I can easily see and change where the app knows I can either rush through breakfast and a shower or skip them, skip playing with my cat and doing Duolingo, but I can’t skip driving to work or make it take less time, etc.) The current system just tries to make every task take a much shorter time without adjusting the end time, and this is not always practical.

The concept of tasks in the routine and the timers is amazing and very helpful, but beyond that it doesn’t feel like the features are as well designed for adults with ADHD to use on the fly as I would like. It does seem to have been overly impacted in its design by the original app that was designed for parents to manage their children’s routines, rather than designed for adults with ADHD to manage their own routines.
author: Anonymous07071

title: Doesn’t make you cancel the free trial
body: I haven’t used the app at all but the fact it doesn’t make you do anything for the free trial and makes you pay only after just proves it has adhd in mind. I hope I can find some success with this and will keep using it if I do.
author: Bib7557865

title: FINALLY
body: A SCHEDULER THAT MAKES SENSE WORTH EVERY PENNY THANKYOU SM
author: Don'tmakemechoose

title: Finally!
body: Something useful. Unlike some of these others..
author: Tall smart cute

title: Schedule and times do not work
body:
There is some bug because

1) I cannot schedule a start and end time. It changes on its own regardless of what time I select. 

2) the set amount of time for activities is in a clock format which doesn’t allow me to select the amount of time for a task. 

3) I want a refund. This app doesn’t work anymore.
author: hturuth

title: Shows promise but needs improvement
body: While this app shows promise, it really needs streamlining in the area of managing routines, especially reordering routines, adjusting times, and easily seeing and fixing time conflicts. Right now I've entered a number of routines, but as I've added in transition times etc that I didn't initially account for, I'm left with time conflicts that are very clunky to resolve. In order to see my daily calendar and identify time conflicts, I have to go to "start routine." To exit that view I have to navigate the Qs of whether I really want to "quit the routine." And then I have to toggle back to "manage routines" to adjust times manually to resolve the conflict. The app shouldn't allow routines to overlap and should automatically adjust times to avoid conflicts. Or, it should easily allow user to view schedule and adjust times where conflicts exist. Also the automatic ordering in "manage routines" based on when you created the routine is the least useful option for how this list could be ordered. Ordering by schedule (like time of day or day of week) would be much better. I still haven't figured out how to reorder this list, in spite of searching support posts. I hope they roll out improvements to this app soon to make it more user friendly to adjust schedules.
author: recleaguebackup

title: Decent app
body:
I wanted to put 3.5 stars. I do love the idea around the app and it’s really user friendly. It’s great how much time I save with it…when I remember to use it. My mornings start early and like most people the first thing on my mind is COFFEE. I don’t remember to “start my routine” until I’m 10 minutes away from leaving for work wondering what I’m forgetting. 

I have noticed with other ADHD apps there are more notifications and not just ‘time remaining in your task’ ones. 
I paused a task because I had to let my dog out and forgot about it until over 3 hours later.

Great app just hoping for some more features
author: SamuraiGirl666

title: Game Changing, but would love a couple of features to be added
body:
This app has been a game changer for me. I’m no longer late for work, and I love having an app that helps me get my routines done, especially when I’m too tired to figure it out myself. I also like the reward system, and the ability to set my own rewards.

Having said that, there are two features that I would love for the developers to add to the app. I use the app on my iPad, and I often have my iPad propped up in landscape mode, which Brili doesn’t use. I really want to be able to use the app in landscape mode. Using the iPad in portrait mode makes it kind of awkward for me. 

The second feature I hope the developer will consider is using different tones for the different task notifications. I often have my iPad set up in one locations, and can’t actually see the app as I’m getting things done on my routine. I like the notification sounds, but I would love to be able to tell if it’s a halfway mark timer, or a 30 seconds left timer. 

Other than these two requests, I love love love this app.
author: S. E. Myers

title: WORTH EVERY PENNY
body: I love Brilli for me and my son. I’ve come back to it again and again bc it’s just one of those apps that really make a difference in your life for the better. It makes being on time and completing all of your tasks easy without missing anything.
author: kendraw850

title: Life changing. Seriously.
body: I cannot recommend this app enough for anyone who has ADHD or suffers from time blindness. I have always been late to EVERYTHING and at 27 I’d just accepted it honestly. But I saw someone mention this app and decided to try it. First of all—a 30 free day trial that AUTOMATICALLY cancels. Not only a generous trial length, but no fear of forgetting to cancel and getting charged!! Honestly so thankful to Brili for that. Routines are customizable and flexible. As long as I have one running I know I’m going to get where I need to be on time! It’s $50 for a year sub, but as someone who was 15 minutes late to EVERY shift… Even on my tipped minimum wage, I am more than making up for that with 15 minutes more on my time card every shift, in wages alone. THANK YOU BRILI!!!
author: DSkye23

title: So frustrated
body:
First, The adult version is still very child like.

Second, It is not intuitive.  Examples… why must I save a task I just changed and then also have to save the routine too or lose my changes.  
Then
I save in the notes but then when I think, oh that’s right, I will need to save task too… nope… so I am punching my phone thinking the save button isn’t working when I need to back page… really!?  No directions just have to figure it out.  
3rd The icons are definitely for children.  You need ones for blood pressure, medicine, find keys, etc.  I looked for blood pressure, and then cuff, and then arm… under arm you have arm chair but nothing that I can recognize as an arm for taking blood pressure… but 
I’m not allowed to use my own icons or pictures. 
4th The swipe seems convoluted.  Sometimes I have to swipe 3 or 4 times before it goes away.
5th If I put a task aside I can only go to the next one on the list.  As adults, we need to be able to change the order easily while the routine is going.
6th The pause feature needs to work better.  If I pause, the timer seems to continue or when I come back, the time starts all over again.  If I have already spent 10 min on a 20 min task and I come back to it and the 20 minute timer starts all over.  I can’t mark it off 5 minutes later when I’m finished because the app says I need to spend 10 minutes on it.  Well I did!!! But the app started the timer over!!! Now, the whole routine isn’t useful, because it’s stuck on this one task that I actually did!  So to fix it, I go back in and have to erase all the minimum minutes so this is a feature that I can’t use! 
Finally, I really wanted to like this app.  In fact this is the second time trying to use it.  I was hopeful this time because the adult version looked promising and hopefully be better suited for adults.  Nope… keep working on it.  I’m canceling my subscription for the second time.
author: mnkinnc

title: Apple watch app please!!!
body:
Amazing app! Helps me get on with my morning routines, get through anxiety attacks, organize my work life. 
Just wish there was an apple watch app.
author: Chenuryatka1

title: So Far It’s Great!
body:
I’ve just downloaded it tonight and I love how I can see a calendar view of the routines I have created. 

Some features I would love to see: 
-tracking of how long it actually takes you to complete tasks so you can refine your routines easily
- an alert when scheduled routines overlap with each other
-the ability to create routines for multiple members of the household so it’s easy to see things like how my routines overlap with my husband’s routines
-a checkbox feature for the notes section of routines so I can create a supply list for that routine 

So far though I am impressed. I hope the app continues to receive updates and gets even better!
author: Sixblueirises

title: Honestly life-changing for ADHD
body: I struggle SO much with sticking to good habits, time blindness, and staying on task because of my adult ADHD, and I cannot stop gushing about Brili to anyone about how amazing and helpful it is. I only wish it allowed you to make quick custom temporary day plans for when there are specific things I need to do in the morning or at work. But for daily things like morning routines and bedtime routines it is incredible and has drastically changed my ability to stay on task and do little things I avoid like washing my face at night. In the app you see that it only takes you 3 minutes, so why not just do it?? Thank you to the developers for making an incredible tool.
author: Ms. Thanksalot

title: Great app, needs Apple Watch compatibility
body: This app has helped me so much with my routines and timing with transitions. Unfortunately, it has tethered me to my smart phone which is the opposite effect I want it to have. Please prioritize making a separate watch app so that users can avoid being distracted by their phone when trying to complete habits and routines
author: cml7xd

title: Game changer for coping with ADHD
body:
This app has changed my life forever. So many of my memories from grade school and onward involve trying to get ready on time in the morning. I’ve even had stress dreams about being hours behind getting ready for something and still not being able to pull myself together. 

Brili has completely changed that. I’ve been using this app daily since February, and while it can be buggy and laggy sometimes, I spend so much less time and mental energy worrying about my morning routines. I even partially attribute the promotion I’ve achieved this year to this app and the increased mental clarity it has provided. 

The monthly subscription is worth it for the flexibility of the app and the absence of ads. Customer support is also responsive and helpful if you run into app errors. 

Seriously, if you have ADHD I would strongly recommend taking the time to set up your daily routines in Brili.
author: jcdonaldson3

title: ADHD Life Changer
body:
I am a very late diagnosed female with ADHD. I’ve never been able to do the timer system for tasks for 2 reasons, 1 because I have no concept of how much time things actually take to do, and 2 timers counting down the set time only further stress me out because I’m then focused on time ticking away instead of the actual task. This app has been a complete game changer for me. Instead of time ticking away, I can see how much time things actually take me to do. Mind blowing. Deep cleaning my kitchen took me 2 hours but only 8 minutes to now deep clean each week. And dishes now only take literally a couple of minutes instead of hours. 

I do wish there was a way to share this among my devices as I currently use my iPhone and iPad interchangeably but don’t want to setup separate apps for each.
author: Simone Wolfe

title: I like this app
body: I like it because it helps me with my morning routine
author: peanutreiley

title: Overall the idea is great, but
body: I wish there would be sounds and notifications like kids’ app has which reminds to stay on task and so on. Otherwise it’s easy to forget that the app was opened. Also having integration with the calendars and notifications on the watch would be helpful. And the list of rewards you can choose from after completing tasks would add some fun and motivation.
author: IiraaTs

title: Not at all a free app
body: If you want a free app, look elsewhere
author: str3ss3dstud3nt

title: Good weekly schedule ideas, but
body: I was excited to find the adult version of the children’s app that was hopefully less glitchy and easy to navigate. Unfortunately, this doesn’t have the main thing I liked about the children’s Brili that virtually no other app has: the ability to move tasks to the end and basically scroll between tasks. Last time I tried it, this only allows you to toggle between two I believe, or briefly put off one task. I know you can completely redo the schedule, but I found that a bit difficult (had a hard time clicking on it or something?). And then that kind of defeats the purpose of being able to *somewhat* mindlessly flip through tasks, while keeping things interesting and flexible. I mentioned this to the creators, but apparently most users, whoever they are, didn’t want that flexibility and preferred to have it this way. The answer seemed pretty final. I might give it another shot someday to see if there are any other updates that make it more usable, and I did like the recommended tasks and schedules as a framework. But I was disappointed after waiting for it to come out heh.
author: Elleoneiram

title: Add Other Routines
body: I would love the option to download other peoples routines as it can be a bit much creating my own routines and the pre made routines that come with the app are limited.
author: goldenroyalty

title: It’s a good app sometimes
body: The app is very helpful when it’s working. But quite often it’s glitchy and will even freeze on a specific task. It requires me to exit the routine and start all over again. I love the app when it’s working but I don’t know why I’m paying so much for this subscription since it so often isn’t working. It makes my ADHD even worse when there’s a barrier to my ability to use what’s keeping me on track.
author: Califoryah

title: Nice 1st impression
body: My first feelings when using the app with a bedtime then a morning routine  were relief because it lessened the anxiety that I wasn’t even truly aware I had, and accomplishment that I could get through all of my tasks in a manageable amount of time because I wasn’t constantly distracted. I was able to relax and move forward quickly and efficiently. I wish there were reports so I could track which tasks habitually take different time then I have scheduled. Also the app has closed mid routine several times and I don’t know if it’s something I’m doing or a glitch in the app.
author: Wordstar

title: Love the app, need watch compatibility
body: I wish when this app was doing crowdfunding it got enough to do the watch app. We have loved this since the original kidnapped by the original designers.It’s absolutely wonderful for ADD or TBI. Unfortunately due to one family members disabilities carrying the phone or iPad around has become extremely difficult and a watch app would literally change everything-fingers crossed it could still happen.
author: J265789

title: Unreliable notifications
body:
When everything is running smoothly this app is GREAT, but it doesn’t always. 

There are some minor things I don’t love, but I can deal with, like the fact that free time always gets added to routines ending at a specific time, even if I’m ending late, or that the app sometimes takes 2-3 minutes to load after tapping a notification, but then counts that time as part of the routine even though it hasn’t shown me what the first task is yet. 

The reason for not continuing to pay though is that anytime I miss even ONE routine I stop getting notifications. I’ve checked all my Apple settings to be sure, but Brili is the only app I have trouble with. 

Like most people who use it I also have ADHD and have not found success with any other app/program/schedule before. This is the only one I’ve ever been able to get myself use with any sort of regularity, but you know how it is with ADHD, if I can’t see it it doesn’t exist. Without notifications letting me know it’s time to start I literally won’t remember to open the app for days at a time.
author: Arandazzo17

title: Life changing but needs Apple Watch feature for 5 stars!
body: Please!
author: caitymccait

title: Such a good app!
body: I absolutely love this app and it makes my day so much more productive! There is one thing, though. I just got this app a few days ago, so I have been editing my routines, and a cool feature that would be useful is if you could move the tasks around without starting your routine. Sometimes I add a task that needs to be listed at the top. If I want to add it to the top, then I have to delete all of the other tasks under where I want to put that one. I tried to rearrange them, but the tasks won’t move up or down. Overall, this app is so useful and easy! I recommend 1000%!!
author: doggyluv0010

title: Apple Watch
body: I love this app! As an adult with adhd it has been incredibly helpful with automating my mornings so that I don’t have to think about what needs to be done next and I don’t get distracted trying to remember what I should be doing. The reminders throughout tasks are great (since I usually get off task midway through the activity) and overall it has made my mornings a lot easier and more productive. I do really wish that there was an Apple Watch feature. It would be great if I could put my phone out of sight but still have the visual reminder of my routine on my watch. Another feature that I think could be a great addition is the ability to add tasks without adding them to a routine permanently. For example if you had a one time change in your schedule, you could add it into your existing routine just for that day but not change any of the other days. Or maybe just a section where you can add activities you would like to do but have no specific date or routine that you could add it to.
author: briiiiiiiiiiiiiiii13555321

title: Voice Notifications?
body: I use the kids’ version of Brili every day and LOVE it! One of the essential pieces of the kids’ app is missing in the adult app. When you swipe to finish an item in the kids’ app, a cheery voice comes on to tell you what to do next. You don’t even have to look at the screen, just listen as you do your tasks. The voice also notifies you when you have a certain amount of time remaining to complete the task. I was so excited to find out that Brili had released an app for adults, but I quickly went back to using the kids’ app because of the voice notifications. I’d love to use the adult app if voice notifications are included!
author: MardelMare

title: Doesn’t work unless screen is on and app is open
body: I get distracted so easily, which is why I need an app like Brili to keep me on task. Therefore, it is extremely frustrating when I turn off my phone screen to get to work, and the app does not let me know when my time is up for my task! It will let me know when I have 30 minutes left, but not when the time is up. Very strange. If the developers could change this so that the alarm goes off whether the app is on the screen, or running in the background, it would be great.
author: Mamacuchara

title: Completely locked out
body: I have been using this app for a bit and there has been no mention of having to pay to use it. This morning I tried to use it and the only thing the app will display is a subscription page that I have never seen before. You can’t navigate away from it. There is no description of what the subscription gives you. My routines have been taken away from me and the only way I can get them back is to fork over money. The app is suddenly, without warning, completely unusable.
author: Doug32148

title: Great redux of kid version!
body:
It has excellent time management features. Brilliant, one of a kind app that compensates for some tasks running long and others running a bit short on any given day In order to get you out the door exactly on time. I recommend this app to a lot of people. 

I have a few suggestions. 
1. The option to have an unscheduled routine. One that has a set duration, rather than time of day. 
2. Make the quote tile card in cockpit optional and/or customizable. I find generic motivational quotes annoying and demoralizing. It made me consider going back to the kids app. 
3. Landscape mode. Really any feature you have on the kids app should be an option on the adult version. 
4. The play button to run a routine outside of the schedule is really unintuitive. I had to look it up. Maybe a big play button in cockpit that says “run a routine” 
5. Make the whole star system optional. 
6. The reward task from the kid app should be in the adult version. It’s nice to build in break time if time allows.
author: ProfessionalArtNerd

title: Please make this for Apple Watch!!!
body: Love this app, it has been life changing for me and my family! The only thing I don’t love is having to carry my phone around while I do chores, it would be so great if there was and Apple Watch version!
author: gentlemomms

title: Just a recommendation
body:
I love this app. I had it for less than a week and I already love it. Now I’m actually remembering to brush my teeth at night 😅 but there is one thing I want there to be. I want there to be a pause button. The time running out makes me anxious. And yes, there is a postpone button, but that just starts the next task and the time starts running out for that. If you could just let me be able to pause the task it I would change to 5 stars.
Thanks.
author: JordIsBored

title: Life-changing app with many improvements! Miss physical rewards.
body:
I started on kids Brili (as an adult) and thought it was AMAZING. I kid you not, Brili is the only thing that has helped streamline and remember my routine in the morning, and get me out the door on time for a change! Before Brili, I’d get so distracted by other things and I felt my morning routine took literally half the day to complete lol. It’s such a relief to have an app like this that just moves me right along. This version of the app brings many needed updates, including the ability to skip or remove tasks from an active routine, which makes it much easier for adults to use than original kid Brili. 

BUT one thing I sorely miss are real world rewards. In kid Brili, you could assign an actual reward (i.e. “ice cream cone” or “video game”) to finishing routines. This version of the app changed rewards to digital achievements (video game style) and I find that way less motivating. I also used to use the physical reward function in kid Brili to curb my impulse spending as well as to motivate completion of routines, so removing it from this version was a double whammy. It’s also caused me to not use the app every day since my under-stimulated ADHD brain thinks it’s not getting rewarded for using it (ugh, the frustration!). If rewards were added back in, this app would be perfect. 

All in all, if you’re struggling with completing routine tasks or time management of your daily routines, you will LOVE this app! Definitely recommend.
author: Kittykat710

title: Absolute life saver
body:
I’m an adult with ADHD—I have terrible “time blindness” and cannot for the life of me get anywhere on time. Unfortunately my job, which I love, is extremely strict about tardiness—even trying my absolute hardest to be on time, I was still getting written up for being three minutes late, or even one minute late. If I was late one more time, I’d be fired. Needless to say, I was at the end of my rope and willing to try anything—even an app for kids. I’m so glad I gave Brili a try—not only have I not been late since using Brili for my morning routine, I consistently leave the house when I plan to (!!) and am EARLY (!!!) every single day. I can get gas on the way to work. I can get a coffee if I want! I feel like I have an incredible new super power—I can understand time 😂 I’m in control of my mornings. 

As much as I wish there wasn’t a monthly subscription fee, it sure beats losing my freaking job! 

Thank you Brili 🙏🏻
author: Reillllow

title: I LOVE THIS APP!!!!!
body: Brili completely changed my life. I’ve been using the kids version of the app for a few years and just switched all my routines to the adult version. The example I give to friends all the time: my least favorite chore is washing dishes and just by adding that one item to my nightly routine, I regularly have a clean kitchen now. FINALLY!!! Who knew that I just needed a little outside reenforcement to help me realize that staying on task doesn’t have to be a mountain of struggle. And believe me, I’ve had some serious struggles just trying to stay afloat with life. I was only officially diagnosed with ADHD a month ago, though I’ve been trying to use ADHD life hacks/tips for the past three years or so because of how much they helped.
author: cansomething

title: What a blessing!
body: I was diagnosed with ADD three years ago at age 55. My medication has been helping but I needed something for accountability to change my behavior. In February 2021, I heard about the brili app while watching a YouTube video. I bought it, created some routines, and began experiencing effective time management. Honestly, it felt both strange and wonderful. I had not ever experienced the success of managing my time well and this feeling was new to me. The longer I use the app, the easier it is for me to stay on task, finish it, then move on to the next one. Every now and then I didn’t use the app and thought I’d manage my day by myself. Big mistake. I use the app every day now and am thankful for it. I get to experience the satisfaction of managing my time well.
author: MinPinMama:)

title: Facebook Group
body: Ran across this App on TikTok! I love the app and it has worked for my ADHD so far. I’d like to share successes and user stories and hopefully add a social aspect to keep the dopamine high. :)
author: AKA zee

title: Promising app but needs more work
body: I love the idea of this app and it’s set up in a way that I can stay on task to get a full routine done! But the movements aren’t intuitive immediately so I ended up making routines and competing them on accident but was unable to delete the completion on my schedule after. I think this app can be really useful but some basic functionality is still lacking
author: megheis

title: A new family member
body: A great addition to our family!  My husband was diagnosed with a cognitive disorder and we’ve been using Brilli for several months with much success.  It keeps him on task and the interface is intuitive which makes the app easy to use.  And recent updates have made the experience better, you can tell the developers understand their user’s needs.

title: Unbelievable
body: This app cracked the code.

title: 5 stars
body: I am an OT and I think this app is extremely helpful for someone with ADHD to get all their self care completed before leaving the house for the day. You can set up your schedule the way you want and then the app reminds you to complete the task.
author: momnotebook

title: Recent Success Story
body: Great app for getting me out of bed and ready for work! I’m excited to see where Brili goes from here.
author: Mare Pen

title: Crowdfunding Supporter to App User
body: I really enjoy the way this app brings me through my morning routine. Since i have downloaded and reported several issues, most have been fixed so it is great to see the team is constantly working to improve. Overall, there is room to grow and I think this app will go from good to great in the next few months!
author: Fashioniseverything

title: Lack of Sync w/other iPad/iPhone causing chaos
body:
This is potentially the leading app of its type. — But the lack of synchronization between devices at this annual cost is bad. I regret purchasing it without that, and cannot recommend it. 

When the app developers can let us know this is resolved, 
i would recommend it.
author: BrightGTR

title: It’s gonna make so much more sense
body: When I recommend this app every time someone tells me how they’re struggling with something. I always say “Listen, I never though Iii would ever have a routine but this app makes it work for me! Now-it’s TECHNICALLY for kids but hear me out...” Honestly-to anyone considering it-this is the ONLY routine app that works for me. I went from being CHRONICALLY LATE to on time and prepared for my days. I feel so much more capable and I make sure to create routines that are satisfying. It helps me understand how long I will ACTUALLY need to do things and if I run behind it adjusts to favor it so that I can stay on track. It keeps me mentally stable and not only able to stick to a routine but wanting to. This app will wholeheartedly change everything you know about routines. I can not recommend it enough.
author: MissAshley86

title: FINALLY
body:
YES. I’ve been using the version for kids for over a year and it fully changed my life, but it always felt a little silly to need to switch back and forth between Laura (parent) and Laura (diminutive) to do anything, so this is a game changer.

One thing I would love to see incorporated is to allow landscape orientation. I like to display it on my iPad with the little foldy stand so keeping it in portrait is a little unwieldy. 

All in all though I am SO EXCITED to give this a go. THANK YOU for making this!!
author: Lllljkhhvdjchcnfgbshvnbxfjcg

title: I wish there were rewards!
body: I had used the brili app for kids before, but I wished there was more flexibility. I just got this one and I love the new features. However I miss the option to set rewards for yourself that was in the kids version. I find it difficult to be motivated without some sort of reward. I hope that in the future the developers might consider adding a reward feature in. Thank you!
author: panda that is red

title: Good system Broken by glitches
body:
The system is great when it works.
But there are consistent glitches that make it difficult and even break it.
For example: when I start the app everyday it starts on the last task of my first routine. So I have to cancel and restart the routine. Today the same thing happened but now the entire app is crashing and is just unusable.

I might try the kids version. Since it’s older it might be more stable.
author: kevinb410
